rule: Plain English: rules 2 and 8; three opening sentences simplified
original: This pull request adds the AMX QK kernel that reads the packed K plane of the layout PR (PR #4868) as the right operand of the tile multiply and computes `S = Q * K^T` directly, without the register transpose (a transpose done in AVX-512 vector registers) of the row-major kernel. This PR removes the layout PR's temporary gate: a dense page of a packed slot takes the AMX page path, and partial pages, the kill switch, hosts without AMX and 128-dimension heads with kv_mul other than 4 keep the AVX-512 reader. The CMake option that selects the layout stays off in every preset, and against `main` the measured decode TPS rises by 5.4 % at prompt length 1,024 tokens and by 9.5 % at 8,192 tokens.
fix: This pull request lets Intel AMX (matrix instructions) read the packed attention keys introduced by PR #4868 without transposing the output scores. In the measured Qwen3-4B model run, generation throughput rises by 5.4 % for a 1,024-token prompt and by 9.5 % for an 8,192-token prompt against `main` at `72308ec90c`. The packed key layout remains disabled in every build preset.

rule: Wade check 6: scope of the measurement
original: With the kill switch, a packed binary packs no query and runs the reader for every page. Without it, a dense page takes the kernel. So this pair measures the cost of the reader against the kernel inside one binary.
fix: With the kill switch, a packed binary packs no query and runs the reader for every page. Without it, eligible dense pages use both AMX kernels. This comparison measures the end-to-end effect of disabling the AMX page path in one binary.

rule: Wade check 6: reader cost is not isolated
original: In this PR the kill switch changes the scoring path of every dense page of a 128-dimension head, from the kernel to the reader. The decode cost of the reader is 11.0 % and 18.3 % of TPS in the two cells. The prefill cost is 674 ms and 64.9 s of TTFT. `newoff` is within 1.3 % of `headoff` in TPS and TTFT in both cells (next subsection). A `new` binary with the switch therefore behaves like the layout PR's binary.
fix: The switch disables query packing and both AMX kernels for eligible dense pages. It also removes tile-region setup. In these two cells, disabling AMX reduces decode throughput by 11.0 % and 18.3 %. It increases TTFT by 674 ms and 64.9 s. These measurements do not isolate the reader's cost. `newoff` is within 1.3 % of `headoff` in TPS and TTFT in both measured cells (next subsection).

rule: Wade check 6: separate observation from cause
original: A difference beyond the band would show that the two binaries differ in work outside the kernel.
fix: A difference beyond the band flags a control difference to investigate. It does not identify its cause.

rule: CI terminology: workflow configuration versus required checks
original: | CI, required CI, legacy CMake lane | CI means continuous integration, the automated build and test system. Required CI is the workflow `gcp-nix.yml`, plus `deb-smoke.yml`, an APT (Debian package manager) package check that builds no tron binary. The C++ test build of `gcp-nix.yml` uses `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix`. The legacy CMake lane is `.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`. It runs by manual dispatch and from `publish-deb.yml`, the package-publishing workflow. |
fix: | CI, GCP Nix, legacy CMake lane | CI means continuous integration, the automated build and test system. GCP Nix is the default build-and-test workflow, `gcp-nix.yml`. The separate `deb-smoke.yml` workflow checks authenticated access to the Debian package repository and builds no tron binary. The C++ test build of GCP Nix uses `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix`. The legacy CMake lane is `.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`. It runs by manual dispatch and from `publish-deb.yml`, the package-publishing workflow. |
